title: Psalms Chapter 107 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 107 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 107 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 107.

questions.question: In Psalms 107, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: O give thanks unto the LORD
Then they cried unto the LORD
He brought them out of darkness
questions.correctAnswer: O give thanks unto the LORD
questions.explanation: The first event mentioned in Psalms 107 is giving thanks to the LORD, as stated in Psalms 107:1.

questions.question: Who are the ones that should say so according to Psalms 107?
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:2 explicitly says that the redeemed of the LORD should say so.

questions.question: From which directions did the LORD gather them?
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:3 states that they were gathered from the east, west, north, and south.

questions.question: What did they find while wandering in the wilderness?
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 107:4, they found no city to dwell in while wandering in the wilderness.

questions.question: What happened to their souls while they were hungry and thirsty?
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:5 states that their souls fainted in them due to hunger and thirst.

questions.question: What did they do in their trouble?
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:6 indicates that they cried unto the LORD in their trouble.

questions.question: What did the LORD do after they cried unto Him?
options: He delivered them out of their distresses
questions.correctAnswer: He delivered them out of their distresses
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:6 states that the LORD delivered them out of their distresses when they cried unto Him.

questions.question: Where did the LORD lead them?
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:7 tells us that the LORD led them forth by the right way to a city of habitation.

questions.question: What should men praise the LORD for?
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:8 expresses that men should praise the LORD for His goodness and wonderful works.

questions.question: Who does the LORD satisfy?
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:9 mentions that the LORD satisfieth the longing soul.

questions.question: What did they rebel against?
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:11 states that they rebelled against the words of God.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD brought them out of darkness.
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:14 confirms that He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death.

questions.question: True or False: Their soul was filled with bitterness.
questions.explanation: The text does not mention bitterness; instead, it speaks of their souls fainting in hunger and thirst.

questions.question: True or False: They were bound in affliction and iron.
questions.explanation: The text states they were in darkness and shadow of death, not that they were bound in affliction and iron.

questions.question: True or False: They found a rich city in the wilderness.
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:4 states they found no city to dwell in while wandering in the wilderness.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 107 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 107 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What has the LORD done according to Psalms 107:16?
options: He hath broken the gates of brass
He hath gathered them from the lands
He hath satisfied the longing soul
He hath commanded the stormy wind
questions.correctAnswer: He hath broken the gates of brass
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 107:16 states, 'For he hath broken the gates of brass, and cut the bars of iron in sunder.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 107:19 promise will happen if someone cries unto the LORD in their trouble?
options: He saveth them out of their distresses
He will punish them for their sins
questions.correctAnswer: He saveth them out of their distresses
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 107:19 states, 'Then they cry unto the LORD in their trouble, and he saveth them out of their distresses.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 107:20, what did the LORD send to heal them?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 107:20 states, 'He sent his word, and healed them, and delivered them from their destructions.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 107:22 encourage people to do?
options: Ignore the goodness of the LORD
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 107:22 states, 'And let them sacrifice the sacrifices of thanksgiving, and declare his works with rejoicing.'

questions.question: What is mentioned in Psalms 107:24 that they see in the deep?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 107:24 states, 'These see the works of the LORD, and his wonders in the deep.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 107:27, how do they feel because of trouble?
options: They are at their wits' end
questions.correctAnswer: They are at their wits' end
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 107:27 states, 'They reel to and fro, and stagger like a drunken man, and are at their wits' end.'

questions.question: What happens in Psalms 107:29 when the LORD makes the storm a calm?
options: They are glad because they be quiet
questions.correctAnswer: They are glad because they be quiet
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 107:30 states, 'Then are they glad because they be quiet; so he bringeth them unto their desired haven.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 107:21 say men should do for the LORD's goodness?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 107:21 states, 'Oh that men would praise the LORD for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men!'

questions.question: According to Psalms 107:17, who are afflicted because of their iniquities?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 107:17 states, 'Fools because of their transgression, and because of their iniquities, are afflicted.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 107:4 describe about those who wandered in the wilderness?
options: They found no city to dwell in
questions.correctAnswer: They found no city to dwell in
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 107:4 states, 'They wandered in the wilderness in a solitary way; they found no city to dwell in.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 107:5 say about their condition while wandering?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 107:5 states, 'Hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted in them.'

questions.question: What is the effect of rebellion against the words of God as stated in Psalms 107:11?
options: They will be brought down with labour
questions.correctAnswer: They will be brought down with labour
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 107:11 states, 'Because they rebelled against the words of God, and contemned the counsel of the most High: Therefore he brought down their heart with labour.'

questions.question: Is it true that the redeemed of the LORD should say so according to Psalms 107:2?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 107:2 states, 'Let the redeemed of the LORD say so, whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the enemy.'

questions.question: Is it false that the LORD only hears those who are righteous, according to Psalms 107:6?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 107:6 speaks of anyone crying to the LORD in trouble, indicating that He hears all in distress.

questions.question: Is it false that the LORD causes people to suffer without reason as stated in Psalms 107:12?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 107:12 indicates that their suffering was a consequence of their rebellion against God.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 107 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 107.

questions.question: According to Psalms 107:33, what transformation does the LORD perform on rivers and watersprings?
options: He turneth rivers into a wilderness, and the watersprings into dry ground
He turneth rivers into wine, and watersprings into oil
He turneth rivers into fire, and the watersprings into smoke
He turneth rivers into blood, and the watersprings into salt
questions.correctAnswer: He turneth rivers into a wilderness, and the watersprings into dry ground
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:33 explicitly states, 'He turneth rivers into a wilderness, and the watersprings into dry ground;' indicating a divine alteration of natural water sources.

questions.question: In Psalms 107:38, what blessing does the LORD bestow on the people?
options: He blesseth them also, so that they are multiplied greatly; and suffereth not their cattle to decrease
He blesseth them with gold and silver, and increases their armies
He blesseth them with peace and long life, and heals their diseases
He blesseth them with wisdom and understanding, and grants them kingship
questions.correctAnswer: He blesseth them also, so that they are multiplied greatly; and suffereth not their cattle to decrease
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 107:38, the LORD blesses the people by multiplying them greatly and preventing the decrease of their cattle, showing His provision.

questions.question: What does Psalms 107:41 say about the LORD's treatment of the poor?
options: Yet setteth he the poor on high from affliction, and maketh him families like a flock
He forsaketh the poor and giveth strength to the proud
He humbles the poor and enriches the wicked
He hides the poor in darkness and brings ruin upon them
questions.correctAnswer: Yet setteth he the poor on high from affliction, and maketh him families like a flock
questions.explanation: The verse Psalms 107:41 tells how the LORD elevates the poor from affliction and makes their families like a flock, indicating divine restoration and care.

questions.question: Which assembly is specifically mentioned in Psalms 107:32 as a place to exalt and praise the LORD?
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:32 states, 'Let them exalt him also in the congregation of the people, and praise him in the assembly of the elders,' highlighting respect for the elders in worship.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Psalms 107:34 for turning a fruitful land into barrenness?
options: For the wickedness of them that dwell therein
Due to a drought caused by sin
questions.correctAnswer: For the wickedness of them that dwell therein
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:34 explains that the fruitful land is turned into barrenness due to the wickedness of its inhabitants, indicating a moral cause for the desolation.

questions.question: According to Psalms 107:43, what will the wise understand if they observe these things?
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:43 says, 'Whoso is wise, and will observe these things, even they shall understand the lovingkindness of the LORD,' indicating a direct link between wisdom and comprehension of God's kindness.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'hesed' (חֶסֶד) in Psalms 107:43 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'hesed' used in Psalms 107:43 is best translated as 'lovingkindness,' denoting steadfast love and covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Psalms 107:33-38 where natural elements are transformed oppositely?
questions.explanation: The passage Psalms 107:33-38 uses chiasm, a literary device where ideas are presented and then reversed, such as rivers turning to wilderness and then wilderness turning to standing water.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of deliverance from distress found in Psalms 107:6?
questions.explanation: John 16:33 echoes the theme of deliverance and peace amid troubles, paralleling Psalms 107:6 where those in distress cry unto the LORD and He delivers them.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book contains a passage that connects with the theme of God's restoration of barren land as in Psalms 107:35?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 35:1 speaks of the desert blossoming and rejoicing, which connects with Psalms 107:35 where wilderness is turned into standing water and dry ground into watersprings.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Psalms 107:31 in the chapter?
options: He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still
Then are they glad because they be quiet; so he bringeth them unto their desired haven
Then they cry unto the LORD in their trouble, and he bringeth them out of their distresses
They reel to and fro, and stagger like a drunken man, and are at their wits' end
questions.correctAnswer: Then are they glad because they be quiet; so he bringeth them unto their desired haven
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:30 immediately precedes 107:31 and states, 'Then are they glad because they be quiet; so he bringeth them unto their desired haven,' setting the context for the call to praise in verse 31.

questions.question: What literary technique is demonstrated by the repeated refrain 'Oh that men would praise the LORD for his goodness' found in Psalms 107?
questions.explanation: The repeated refrain in Psalms 107 (verses 8, 15, 21, 31) forms an inclusio, a literary framing device that brackets the psalm and emphasizes the theme of praising the LORD.

questions.question: How does Psalms 107:40 illustrate a reversal of fortunes among leaders?
options: He poureth contempt upon princes, and causeth them to wander in the wilderness, where there is no way
He exalts princes to rule with justice and mercy
He blesses princes with wealth and power
He protects princes from their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: He poureth contempt upon princes, and causeth them to wander in the wilderness, where there is no way
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:40 describes how the LORD pours contempt upon princes and causes them to wander aimlessly, illustrating a divine humbling of worldly rulers.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is thematically connected to the healing and deliverance mentioned in Psalms 107:20?
questions.explanation: Exodus 15:26 speaks of God as the healer who will put none of the diseases on His people, connecting with Psalms 107:20's theme of healing and deliverance through God's word.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 107:42 states that all iniquity shall stop her mouth when the righteous see God's works.
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:42 clearly states, 'The righteous shall see it, and rejoice: and all iniquity shall stop her mouth,' confirming the truth of the statement.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 107 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 107 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 107:9 teach about God's provision for the human soul?
options: God satisfies and fills the longing and hungry soul with goodness
God only provides spiritual nourishment, not physical
God punishes the soul for its longings
God ignores the needs of the hungry soul
questions.correctAnswer: God satisfies and fills the longing and hungry soul with goodness
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:9 states, 'For he satisfieth the longing soul, and filleth the hungry soul with goodness,' teaching God's gracious provision for both spiritual and physical needs.

questions.question: What doctrine about human rebellion and divine judgment is taught in Psalms 107:11?
options: Rebellion against God's word results in affliction and bondage
Rebellion brings immediate forgiveness without consequences
God overlooks human rebellion without judgment
Human rebellion leads to divine favoritism
questions.correctAnswer: Rebellion against God's word results in affliction and bondage
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:11 explains that those who 'rebelled against the words of God' are bound in affliction and iron, showing that sin brings consequences.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning divine healing and deliverance is expressed in Psalms 107:20?
options: God sends His word to heal and deliver from destruction
God heals only through human effort and medicine
Deliverance is unrelated to God's word
Healing is a random event without divine involvement
questions.correctAnswer: God sends His word to heal and deliver from destruction
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:20 states, 'He sent his word, and healed them, and delivered them from their destructions,' emphasizing God's active role in healing via His word.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 107:1 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:1 declares 'for his mercy endureth for ever,' highlighting God's enduring mercy.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Psalms 107:25 by God commanding the stormy wind?
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:25 shows God commanding and raising the stormy wind, demonstrating His sovereign control over nature.

questions.question: How does Psalms 107 prepare for the New Testament theme of salvation and deliverance?
options: By illustrating God's deliverance from distress as a type of Christ's salvation
By focusing exclusively on Old Testament covenant law
By denying any future redemption beyond Israel
By emphasizing human works over divine grace
questions.correctAnswer: By illustrating God's deliverance from distress as a type of Christ's salvation
questions.explanation: Psalms 107 repeatedly depicts God rescuing from distress (e.g., v.6, v.13), prefiguring the ultimate deliverance through Christ (cf. Luke 4:18).

questions.question: How does Psalms 107:33-36 connect to the biblical theme of God's providential restoration?
options: It shows God transforming barrenness to fruitfulness, echoing restoration themes in Isaiah
It denies God's involvement in nature
It predicts a permanent curse on the land without hope
It emphasizes human effort as the sole cause of restoration
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God transforming barrenness to fruitfulness, echoing restoration themes in Isaiah
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:33-36 describes God's power to change wilderness into fertile land, paralleling Isaiah's prophecies of restoration (Isaiah 35).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 107:6 and 107:13 teach about salvation?
options: God delivers His people when they cry out in trouble
Salvation is earned by human merit
Deliverance is a natural consequence of luck
questions.correctAnswer: God delivers His people when they cry out in trouble
questions.explanation: Both verses show that crying unto the LORD in trouble results in deliverance, emphasizing God's responsive salvation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 107:29 and 107:30 teach about God's control over creation and human experience?
options: God commands the storm to be calm and leads to safety, showing His control over chaos and providence
Nature is uncontrollable and indifferent to prayer
Human beings control the storms, not God
The storm remains a symbol of divine wrath without relief
questions.correctAnswer: God commands the storm to be calm and leads to safety, showing His control over chaos and providence
questions.explanation: Verses 29-30 depict God calming storms and bringing sailors to a desired haven, illustrating His providential care.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine discipline and restoration do Psalms 107:39 and 107:41 teach?
options: God allows affliction but also exalts the poor, demonstrating both judgment and grace
Affliction is unrelated to divine activity
Restoration comes from human achievement alone
questions.correctAnswer: God allows affliction but also exalts the poor, demonstrating both judgment and grace
questions.explanation: Verse 39 describes affliction and sorrow, while verse 41 shows God exalting the poor, indicating a cycle of discipline and mercy.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 107:23-30 promotes superstition about storms rather than faith in God. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It teaches God's sovereign control over nature and His power to deliver those who cry to Him
It encourages fear of natural elements as autonomous powers
It suggests that storms are random and cannot be influenced by God
It implies that human skill at sea is the only factor in survival
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches God's sovereign control over nature and His power to deliver those who cry to Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:23-30 shows sailors crying to God in distress and God calming the storm, emphasizing divine sovereignty, not superstition.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 107:17 teach about the consequences of sin?
options: Fools are afflicted because of transgression and iniquity
Only external punishment matters, not affliction
Sin leads to immediate divine acceptance
questions.correctAnswer: Fools are afflicted because of transgression and iniquity
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:17 explicitly states that fools suffer affliction due to their sin, affirming the doctrine of divine discipline.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Psalms 107:42 by the righteous rejoicing and iniquity silenced?
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:42 shows the righteous rejoicing and iniquity stopping its mouth, highlighting God's just governance.

questions.question: How do Psalms 107:31 and 107:32 together emphasize corporate worship and testimony?
options: They call for praising God publicly in assemblies, highlighting communal thanksgiving
They focus only on private prayer without public expression
They discourage public praise in favor of silence
They require sacrifices without verbal praise
questions.correctAnswer: They call for praising God publicly in assemblies, highlighting communal thanksgiving
questions.explanation: Verse 31 calls for praise of God's goodness, and verse 32 urges exaltation in the congregation, underscoring corporate worship.

questions.question: What theological significance does Psalms 107:3 have regarding the scope of God's redemption?
options: God redeems people from all directions of the earth, indicating universal reach
God redeems only one ethnic group exclusively
God's redemption is limited to a single city
God redeems only those who never wander
questions.correctAnswer: God redeems people from all directions of the earth, indicating universal reach
questions.explanation: Psalms 107:3 speaks of God gathering people from east, west, north, and south, illustrating the universal extent of redemption.
